speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; please tell me, when did these symptoms start and on what scale is the pain rated from 1 to 10?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (esophageal rupture).

The clinical picture of forceful vomiting following excessive alcohol intake, followed by sudden choking, coughing, and chest pain, is classic for this life-threatening condition. I am requesting immediate confirmation with a water-soluble contrast esophagram. REQUEST TEST: Esophagram (Water-soluble contrast); REQUEST IMAGES: Chest CT with oral and IV contrast.
